Propensity model sensitivity of a matched design

Source: R/propensity_sensitivity.R
propensity_sensitivity.Rd

The one-call diagnostic. It refits the propensity model with every algorithm of the model set, re-matches with the analyst's matching options, applies the quality gate, and reports rank disagreement (the primary summary), pair instability (the second summary of the same gated set: 1 minus the pair recurrence across models; exploratory), the bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model, control spread and pair recurrence, and study-level balance spread. No outcome is used. Rank disagreement is a study-level diagnostic; read it for the study as a whole, not per patient. The diagnostics are evaluated in a manuscript in preparation. When fewer than two models pass the quality gate, print() and summary() say so first: the diagnostic is then outside the setting where it was evaluated.

Usage

propensity_sensitivity(
  x,
  data = NULL,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "bart", "grf_probability"),
  seeds = 1:3,
  folds = 5,
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  n_trees = NULL,
  quality_tolerance = 0.05,
  balance_rule = c("relative", "absolute", "relative_only"),
  balance_margin = 0.1,
  balance_cap = 0.25,
  balance_threshold = 0.1,
  bootstrap_samples = 20,
  covariates = NULL,
  replace = FALSE,
  m_order = "largest",
  caliper = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  seed = 1
)

# S3 method for class 'propensity_sensitivity'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'propensity_sensitivity'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.propensity_sensitivity'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'propensity_sensitivity'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A matchit object (from MatchIt::matchit()) or a two-sided formula such as treat ~ x1 + x2. Only baseline covariates belong in the formula; exclude outcomes, identifiers and post-treatment variables (for example, treat ~ . - death - id).

data

The data frame. Required with a formula; with a matchit object it is looked up from the object's call when NULL.

algorithms

The propensity model set. The default is the set evaluated in a manuscript in preparation: logistic regression, BART and the GRF probability forest (with the default seeds, three seeds for each tree algorithm: seven models; packages 'dbarts' and 'grf'). A faster set is available with algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"); it is not part of that evaluation. See fit_propensity_models() for every option and the fixed settings.

seeds, folds, cross_fit, n_trees, quality_tolerance

Passed to fit_propensity_models(). n_trees applies to gradient boosting only.

balance_rule

The balance part of the quality gate: "relative" (default), "relative_only" (the relative rule without the cap) or "absolute". See Steps.

balance_margin, balance_cap

Relative rule: a model fails if its post-match maximum absolute standardized mean difference on main terms is more than balance_margin above the best model's (default 0.10) or above balance_cap (default 0.25; not used by "relative_only").

balance_threshold

Absolute rule: largest allowed post-match maximum absolute standardized mean difference on main terms (default 0.10). Used only with balance_rule = "absolute".

bootstrap_samples

Number of logistic bootstrap refits, for the bootstrap rank instability and the bootstrap pair recurrence (default 20; 0 for none).

covariates

Data frame of covariates for the control spread and the balance statistics. Its rows must be the same patients in the same order as data; when both have row names other than the default and they differ, the function stops. NULL (default) uses the source columns of the formula's right-hand side, from data, resolved with R's formula rules: . means every other column and exclusions such as - death are respected; I(age^2) gives age, age:diabetes gives age and diabetes.

replace, m_order, caliper

Matching options for the formula interface (without replacement, order "largest", no caliper by default; the caliper is in standard deviations of each model's logit). With a matchit object they are read from the object and must not be given.

cores

Number of cores (default 1).

seed

Integer seed from which every other seed is derived.

digits

Significant digits for printed numbers.

...

Not used.

object

A propensity_sensitivity object.

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for the generic.

Value

An object of class "propensity_sensitivity": a list with patients (one row per patient: id, treated, rank_disagreement, rank_disagreement_between, rank_disagreement_within, logit_disagreement, control_spread, control_spread_scaled, pair_recurrence_models, pair_recurrence_bootstrap, outside_support, logistic_score; the treated-only measures are NA for untreated patients), models (one row per model plus the reference row), summary (a table of the study-level numbers with and without the gate, plus flags), quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models, balance_spread (spread tables with and without the gate), bootstrap_rank_instability (see bootstrap_rank_instability(); NULL without bootstrap refits; its study-level value is also the row bootstrap_rank_instability_treated of the summary table; the summary table also has pair_instability_models_mean_treated, 1 minus pair_recurrence_models_mean_treated), settings and components (the model set and the match set). components$model_set is the fitted fit_propensity_models() object, with every model's cross-fitted probability, logit and rank, so that its scores can be reused (for example in another estimator) without refitting; summary$models_used names the models in use.

Steps

  1. fit_propensity_models() with the formula (cross-fitted scores by default).

  2. match_each_model() with the matching options and the logistic bootstrap block.

  3. balance_spread() for every model.

  4. Final quality gate: passed_quality_gate = passed_logloss_gate & smd_max_main <= balance_limit. With the default balance_rule = "relative" the limit is the smallest max |SMD| on main terms among the refitted models plus balance_margin (0.10), and never above balance_cap (0.25): a model is excluded only when its balance is clearly worse than the best model's. With balance_rule = "relative_only" the limit is the best model's value plus balance_margin, without the cap; use it as a sensitivity analysis when the cap excludes every model (many covariates). With balance_rule = "absolute" the limit is balance_threshold (0.10). If fewer than two models pass, every model is used and quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models is TRUE (applied to the final set).

  5. rank_disagreement(), control_spread(), pair_recurrence() and the balance spread on the final set (summary column with_gate) and on every model (without_gate).

Reading a matchit object

From a matchit object the function reads the formula, the method, ratio, replace, m.order (from the call; MatchIt's default for the ATT with a propensity score is "largest") and the caliper. Only 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching on a propensity score for the ATT is supported, with or without replacement and with or without a caliper on the score; anything else stops with a clear error. MatchIt applies a caliper in standard deviations of the analyst's distance (over all patients); the same number of standard deviations is applied to the logit of every model here. When data is NULL the data is found by evaluating the object's data argument in the calling frame.

Reference model

The analyst's own score (x$distance) is kept as the reference model, an extra row of models with model_id = "reference". Its ranks come from x$distance (ranks do not depend on the scale) and its balance statistics from x$weights. Its log-loss, Brier score and c-statistic are NA: it is an in-sample score from the user's object and is not comparable with the cross-fitted scores. Its quality gate is judged on balance only; when it fails, the row is flagged "reference model outside the equally-reasonable set". It is never one of the models in use. summary reports its mean absolute rank difference from the models in use, over treated patients: the mean over treated i and models m of |r_ref(i) - r_m(i)|.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
matched <- MatchIt::matchit(treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
                            data = lalonde, distance = "glm", link = "linear.logit",
                            replace = TRUE)
# A fast model set for this example; the default set is slower (see below).
sensitivity <- propensity_sensitivity(
  matched, algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"),
  seeds = 1, n_trees = 100, bootstrap_samples = 5
)
sensitivity
#> Propensity model sensitivity
#> WARNING: fewer than two models passed the quality gate; the diagnostic is outside the setting where it was evaluated.
#> Every model is used below, so the values do not describe a set of equally good models. Do not read them as a validated result.
#> 1. Quality gate: 3 of 3 models in use (3 algorithms: logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting); log-loss within 5 % of the best; relative balance rule: max |SMD| main terms at most 0.1 above the best model's and <= 0.25, limit here 0.25
#>    Fewer than two models passed, so every model is used. Failed:
#>      logistic_regression_1: log-loss above (1 + quality_tolerance) x best; max |SMD| main terms more than balance_margin above the best model's or above balance_cap
#>      gradient_boosting_1: max |SMD| main terms more than balance_margin above the best model's or above balance_cap
#> 2. Rank disagreement (study mean over treated): 0.0687; median between/within ratio NA (exploratory; near 1 = seed noise)
#>    Pair instability across the models in use (study mean over treated; exploratory): 0.6
#>    Bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model (study mean over treated): 0.0361
#> 3. Balance spread (range of max |SMD| main terms across the models in use): 0.125 (0.16 to 0.285)
#> Mean scaled control spread over treated (descriptive): 1.19 (1 = controls differ as much as a typical match differs from its treated patient)
#> Treated kept: 100 % (lowest model in use)

summary(sensitivity)
